title: Global Leadership Challenge 2026
organization: Global Leadership Challenge (with the St. Gallen Symposium)
overview: Five half-days in December 2026 in which 100 selected young leaders work in teams on real challenges set by partner organisations. The three best teams are invited to the St. Gallen Symposium in Switzerland in April 2027, all expenses covered.
program_dates: Challenge: 10-14 December 2026 (around five half-days). Winners: 56th St. Gallen Symposium, April 2027.
deadline_text: Application Closes: 5 November 2026. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, so don't wait until the deadline.
funding_details: The three winning teams attend the 56th St. Gallen Symposium in April 2027 as Leaders of Tomorrow: 'their expenses for travel and accommodation will be fully covered'
Nothing on the pages read mentions a fee for taking part in the challenge itself
eligibility: A student currently enrolled in a Master's or PhD programme, or a young professional aged between 21 and 30
Demonstrated commitment to responsible leadership through extra-curricular activities and/or work experience
Available for around five half-days from 10 to 14 December 2026
nationality_requirements: No nationality restriction stated; the 2025 edition had participants from more than 80 countries
application_process: Apply on the official site before 5 November 2026 (rolling review)
Upload the documents requested in the form
eligibility_reason: A graduate under 30 who is starting a career counts as a young professional aged 21 to 30. The application must also show commitment to responsible leadership through activities or work.
potential_issues: Only the three winning teams travel; the other participants take part in the challenge without a funded trip
Whether the December sessions are online is implied by the half-day format but not stated on the pages read
A Schengen visa would be needed for Switzerland if selected for the Symposium
benefits: Work on real challenges from partner organisations
Senior advisers and a 100-person international cohort
Chance of a funded trip to the St. Gallen Symposium
relevance_reason: The age rule and the 'young professional' category fit without any degree-enrolment condition, and team problem-solving on business challenges suits a business graduate.

visa.required: Only for winners travelling to Switzerland

action: Apply early, since review is rolling, and keep 10 to 14 December free.
notes: Aggregators title this 'University of Oxford x St. Gallen Symposium Global Leadership Challenge'; the Oxford link was not checked on the official site.

title: Internet Society Fellowship Program 2027
overview: Structured fellowship combining training, mentorship and a funded project, plus travel support to attend a global or regional Internet event. Anyone who completes the free pre-fellowship training by 22 November 2026 receives the application link.
country: Online, with travel to an Internet event
program_dates: Kick-off 22 February 2027; mentored project 1 June to 30 November 2027; final delivery 3 December 2027
deadline_text: Complete all required Pre-Fellowship Training modules before 22 November 2026; fellowship applications close 18 December 2026 and are accepted on a rolling basis.
funding_details: A project stipend of up to USD 5,000, upon approval of the project budget
Travel support to attend a global or regional Internet event (for example IGF, AfPIF or the NDSS Symposium)
Mentorship and expert sessions
stipend: Project stipend of up to USD 5,000
eligibility: Enrol in and complete the Pre-Fellowship Training before 22 November 2026
Choose a track: Internet Policy and Mobilization, Internet Connectivity, or Internet Safety and Security
High level of reading, speaking and writing skills in English
nationality_requirements: No nationality restriction stated on the page read
application_process: 23 September to 22 November 2026: self-paced pre-fellowship training
Application link emailed within 24 hours of completing the modules
eligibility_reason: The route in is the free training, which anyone can take, and English is at professional level. Selection then depends on proposing a credible project in one of the three tracks.
potential_issues: The training must be finished before 22 November 2026
A concrete Internet-related project is needed
The subject is far from the recorded experience
benefits: Travel to an international Internet event
relevance_reason: The policy track is the natural entry for someone with public-sector research experience, and the open training route makes it unusually accessible.
action: Enrol in the pre-fellowship training now and decide after the first modules whether you have a project idea.

title: ICANN Fellowship Program
organization: ICANN (Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers)
overview: Fellows receive training, a mentor and travel assistance to attend an ICANN Public Meeting. The round opening in November 2026 is reserved for past fellows; the next round for first-time applicants has not been announced.
program_dates: ICANN meetings: 13-18 March 2027 (Community Forum) and 14-17 June 2027 (Policy Forum)
deadline_text: The round for the ICANN88 Community Forum is closed. The round for the ICANN89 Policy Forum opens 5 November 2026 and closes 5 December 2026, but only Fellowship alumni may apply for a Policy Forum fellowship.
funding_details: 'Travel assistance to attend the meeting is also provided.' Components are not itemised on the page read.
eligibility: At least 21 years of age when applying
Interested in, or already engaged in, ICANN's work on policy, the Domain Name System and Internet security and stability
Not involved in another ICANN-supported travel programme at the time of selection
nationality_requirements: No nationality restriction stated on the page read
application_process: Apply online during the round for a given ICANN meeting
eligibility_reason: The only stated conditions are being 21 or older and showing interest in ICANN's work, but nothing in the profile shows engagement with Internet governance yet.
potential_issues: No round currently open to first-time applicants
Needs a demonstrated interest in domain names and Internet policy
benefits: Travel to an ICANN Public Meeting
relevance_reason: A travel-funded route few people consider, though it is a stretch for a business profile without Internet-governance activity.
action: Low priority. Pair it with the Internet Society training if that field interests you.

program_dates: The 2026 Forum covered 24 August to 4 September; 2027 dates not announced
deadline_text: No 2027 call yet. For the 2026 Forum: 'The European Forum Alpbach application platform will open from 2-22 March 2026.'

funding_details: A scholarship covers the participation fee for the entire Forum and accommodation

eligibility: Up to the age of 30; up to 35 for applicants from the Global South, which by the UNCTAD definition includes Africa
Applicants from all countries and professional or academic backgrounds
age_requirement: Up to 30, or up to 35 for applicants from the Global South
application_process: Apply on the Forum's application platform during the March window
Ask for an advanced scholarship in the same application if travel costs are a barrier
eligibility_reason: Applicants from Africa are accepted up to age 35 and from any background, which the profile meets.

The advanced scholarship lump sum is awarded only to those with the greatest need

participation_fee: Application fee of USD 24.24, according to the listing

nationality_requirements: Listed as open to all countries
